chunks: From him, from Safwan ibn Hakim, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
When you pray at the tree, do not recite the Talbiyah aloud until you reach Al-Bayda', where the people say 'The earth swallows the army'.

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَة: The declaration of pilgrimage (Labbayk Allahumma labbayk)
key_terms.الْبَيْدَاء: Al-Bayda', a specific location on the road to Mecca
key_terms.يَخْسِفُ بِالْجَيْشِ: The earth swallows the army (referring to the event of Qarun or the Army of the Elephant)

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrist stop reciting the Talbiyah aloud during the Hajj journey?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-istibsar highlights the Shia practice of keeping the Talbiyah quiet (khufiyan) until passing the tree of Dhul Hulaifa, distinguishing it from the public declaration (jahr) often associated with other schools. The reference to Al-Bayda' and the 'swallowing of the army' alludes to the historical event of the Year of the Elephant, serving as a geographical and spiritual marker for pilgrims to transition from the state of ihram preparation to the full performance of Hajj rituals.
